protections: P1: initial component data JSON is escaped by sanitize_html ('<' -> \u003C, '>' -> \u003E, '&' -> \u0026) before being written into a <script type="application/json"> element (django_unicorn/utils.py:137-147; django_unicorn/components/unicorn_template_response.py:93-96).

P2: the rendered component HTML is parsed and re-serialized by BeautifulSoup, whose HTMLFormatter entity-substitutes text and attribute values (django_unicorn/components/unicorn_template_response.py:20-27,70,117-118,126-128).
P3: component templates are rendered through Django's template engine with autoescape, so {{ attr }} values are escaped (django_unicorn/components/unicorn_view.py:294-324,384-397).
P4: form validation messages are produced with escape_html=True before being returned (django_unicorn/components/unicorn_view.py:422).

P5: client code writes server strings through DOM properties/attributes (el.value, setAttribute) and morphdom instead of innerHTML/eval for data values (django_unicorn/static/unicorn/js/element.js:308-324,329-332; messageSender.js:206-215).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The component id is normally a shortuuid, and child ids are hashed when settings.DEBUG is false, so the id looks server-generated; the advisory's reported data is already sanitized by the JSON <script> path, so this adjacent inline-script context is easy to leave alone.

conflicts.what: Escaping the shared component id for HTML (sanitize_html/escape) changes the value used by document.getElementById in the inline script and by unicorn:id/unicorn:key matching; T1 needs JS-string escaping (e.g. django.utils.html.escapejs) that decodes back to the raw id, while the id attribute must stay the raw value.

An attribute allowlist that stops the client from setting calls closes T6's client route into T5, but the component-code route (self.call(...)) remains; simply dropping calls from the response would break the documented JavaScript-calling feature (js.py:17-21, tests/templatetags/test_unicorn_render.py:242-269).

fairness_risks: Component ids are not free-form: child ids are built as parent:name[:key] (templatetags/unicorn.py:110-134) and ids are used as DOM ids, cache keys and selector values (unicorn_view.py:167; messageSender.js:187-199). A rule that bans ':' '.' '/' or quotes would break legitimate nested components and partial targeting.

Values must round-trip unchanged from the initial JSON through JSON.parse back into form controls (component.js:408-444; element.js:308-324); escaping data values instead of the JSON text would corrupt legitimate user text containing <, > or & (e.g. code typed into a textarea).

sanitize_html's \u003C/\u003E/\u0026 escapes must stay valid JSON so JSON.parse yields the original characters (utils.py:146; tests/test_utils.py:67-71); a fix that HTML-entity-escapes values would change what the client sees.

syncInput is a documented feature used for nested models and toggles (action_parsers/utils.py:45-125; action_parsers/call_method.py:69-74); any allowlist must still permit declared public attributes and dotted paths such as flavor.name.

design.why: T1 (with its nested/AJAX route T2) is the only production-reachable server-side XSS sink: the component id is concatenated raw into the inline <script type="module"> even though the same value is safely placed in the JSON script tag, and the `id`/`key`/`model` template kwargs bypass the shortuuid/DEBUG hashing (unicorn_view.py:161-163). T6 is the one independent missing guard (unchecksummed syncInput can set internal attributes such as calls/template_name and the check decides on data, not on the action queue/id). That makes two independent groups with different reasons to dismiss (id looks server-generated; syncInput is the public API), below the 3-5 required; the attribute path T3 is already covered by BeautifulSoup serialization and does not add a real group, so this candidate does not support a full stacked task even though T1 alone is a strong hard/xhard trap.
